title: Three South Jersey Grads Returning Home for 2026 MAAC Tournament - NewsBreak
text:
By Josh Hennig ,
5 hours ago
The 2026 edition of the MAAC Men’s and Women’s Basketball Tournaments return to Jim Whelan Boardwalk Hall in Atlantic City for six days of basketball action. The winner of each tournament gets an automatic qualifying bid to the NCAA Tournament and are in the running for the National Championship.
After the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC) signed a new . But a new multiyear media rights agreement for multiplatform broadcasting of sporting events with ESPN, there is a new schedule of games for the 2026 edition of their college basketball tournament.
Starting on Thursday, March 5th , there will be four days of single elimination play culminating with the Women’s Championship game on Monday, March 9th, and the Men’s Championship Game on Tuesday, March 10th.
Three South Jersey High School Graduates at Boardwalk Hall for 2026 MAAC Tournaments On the same weekend there will be four South Jersey Boxers in action down the street at Tropicana Atlantic City , people can also come out and support these South Jersey High School Alumni who will be in action with their MAAC Basketball Teams:
* Marist Guard Kasey Bretones (Mainland Regional High School)
-Thursday, March 5th – Women’s First Round (Game 1) – No. 8 Manhattan vs. No. 9 Marist at 12:00 PM
-The 5’11” Sophmore was voted the MVP of the Cape Atlantic League Tournament in her junior and senior years of High School. After transferring from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, Bretones has carved out a role in the Marist backcourt rotation. She has 16 Steals in 19 games played this season
* Merrimack Forward David Munro (Camden High School)
-Friday, March 6th – Men’s Quarterfinals (Game 3) – No. 1 Merrimack vs. Winner Game 1 at 6:00 PM
-The Freshman averaged 19 Points per game his senior year of High School, and was named New Jersey Athletics All-State Second-Team.
* Merrimack Guard Tye Dorset (Lenape High School)
-Friday, March 6th – Men’s Quarterfinals (Game 3) – No. 1 Merrimack vs. Winner Game 1 at 6:00 PM
-The 6’3″ Sophomore is in his first year as a starter, averaging 11.9 Points per Game and 1.82 Steals per game this season. Dorset has played in 50 games over the last two years for a Merrimack team that is 39-25 during his time playing at the school.
KEEP READING: South Jersey Athletes Who Played/Coached in NBA and MLB Gallery Credit: Josh Hennig Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Malik Allen This Shawnee High School Graduate played College Basketball at Villanova. Malik Allen played 478 games in the NBA for the Miami Heat (2001-2005), Charlotte Hornets (2005), Chicago Bulls (2005-2007), New Jersey Nets (2007-08), Dallas Mavericks (2008), Milwaukee Bucks (2008-09), Denver Nuggets (2009-10), and Orlando Magic (2010-11). Since 2019, Malik Allen has been a member of the Miami Heat Coaching Staff. Previous, he was a coach with the Minnesota Timberwolves (2018-2019), and Detroit Pistons (2014-2018). Photo by David Maxwell/Getty Images Mike Trout Mike Trout, a graduate from Millville High School, was selected by the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim in the 1st Round of the 2009 MLB Draft. Trout has played 13 seasons for the Angels, winning three American League MVP Awards, two All-Star Game MVP Awards, and was selected to eleven MLB All-Star Games. Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images Chris Ford Sr. Chris Ford Senior graduated from Holy Spirit High School and played College Basketball at Villanova. Ford was selected by the Detroit Pistons in the 2nd Round of the 1972 NBA Draft. Ford played 11 seasons in the NBA for the Pistons and Celtics. Ford was a member of the 1980-81 NBA Championship team. After his NBA career, Ford several seven seasons as an Assistant Coach with the Celtics and would go on to serve as an NBA Head Coach for 10 seasons with the Celtics, Milwaukee Bucks, Los Angeles Clippers, and Philadelphia 76ers. Photo by Denis Poroy/Getty Images Matt Szczur Matt Szczur was a Football and Baseball star player at Lower Cape May Regional before attending Villanova where he won an FCS National Football Championship. He was selected by the Chicago Cubs in the 5th Round of the 2010 MLB Draft. Szczur has played in five MLB seasons with the Cubs and Padres; he was a member of the 2016 World Series Championship team. Photo by Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images Lou Roe Lou Roe, a graduate from Atlantic City High School, was the1994-95 A-10 Player of the Year and Consensus All-American 2nd Team at the University of Massachusetts. Roe was the 30th overall pick by the Detroit Pistons in the 1995 NBA Draft. Roe appeared in 66 NBA games over two seasons for the Pistons and Warriors. Brett Kennedy After graduating from Atlantic City High School and pitching at Fordham University, Brett Kennedy was selected by the San Diego Padres in the 11th Round of the 2015 MLB Draft. Kennedy started six games for the Padres during the 2018 MLB season. But after sustaining multiple injuries, he was relegated to the Minor Leagues for the next four years. Kennedy made his return to the Major Leagues in 2023 when he pitched in five games for the Cincinnati Reds. Photo by Doug Benc/Getty Images Dennis Horner Dennis Horner is a graduate from Holy Spirit High School and played College Basketball at North Carolina State. Horner was signed as an Undrafted Free Agent by the New Jersey Nets in 2011. Horner appeared in Eight Games for the Nets during the 2011-12 season. Photo by Rob Tringali/Getty Images Darren Ford Darren Ford is a graduate from Vineland High School and was drafted by the Milwaukee Brewers in the 18th Round of the 2004 MLB Draft. Ford was traded by the Brewers to the Giants in 2008 and played in 33 games for San Francisco during the 2010 and 2011 seasons. Also, Darren's Grandfather played in MLB too: Ted Ford, also a graduate from Vineland High School, played for the Indians and Rangers from 1970 to 1973. Photo by Lintao Zhang/Getty Images Jason Thompson The Lenape High School Alumni played his College Basketball at Rider University before he was selected with the 12th overall pick in the 2008 NBA Draft. Jason Thompson played seven seasons with the Sacramento Kings (2008-2015). Thompson also spent time playing with the Golden State Warriors and Toronto Raptors during his 8-year NBA career, Thompson is top ten in Kings' Franchise History in Game Played (541), Total Rebounds (3,746) and Blocked Shots (394). Photo by Harry How/Getty Images Frank Vogel Frank Vogel is a graduate from Wildwood High School and was a Student Manager for the University of Kentucky Men's Basketball team when Rick Pitino was coaching the Wildcats. Vogel began his NBA career as a Video Coordinator with the Boston Celtics hired by Pitino. Vogel would go on to work as an Assistant Coach for the 76ers, Advance Scout for the Lakers, and then an Assistant Coach with the Pacers before becoming Indiana's Interim Head Coach in 2011. Vogel worked as the Head Coach with the Pacers for 6 seasons and the Orlando Magic for 2 seasons. He won an NBA Championship as the Head Coach for the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020. After three years coaching the Lakers, Vogel became the Head Coach of the Phoenix Suns for the 2023-24 NBA season. Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Cody Stashak Cody Stashak, a graduate from Oakcrest High School and selected by the Minnesota Twins in the 13th Round of the 2015 MLB Draft. Stashak appeared in 18 games for the Twins during the 2019 season along with pitching in 2 games in the 2019 postseason. After sustaining a season ending Shoulder Injury in 2022, Stashak was not brought back to the Twins organization. The Oakcrest High School Graduate signed a Minor League deal with the San Francisco Giants ahead of the 2024 MLB season. Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Pops Mensah-Bonsu A graduate from Saint Augustine Prep, Pops Mensah-Bonsu played College Basketball at George Washington before signing as an Undrafted Free Agent with the Dallas Mavericks in 2006. He played in a total of 61 NBA games for the Mavericks, Spurs, Raptors, Rockets, and New Orleans Hornets. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Buddy Kennedy A graduate from Millville High School, Buddy Kennedy was selected in the 5th round of the 2017 MLB Draft by the Arizona Diamondbacks. Kennedy appeared in 40 games for the D-Backs from 2022-2023.
The Infielder spent the first half of the 2024 season with the Detroit Tigers (appearing in 6 games) before being traded to the Philadelphia Phillies. Kennedy has played in 60 games at the Phillies Triple-A Affiliate in 2024. Photo by Stephen Dunn/Getty Images Dajuan Wagner One of the best High School Basketball Players in New Jersey history, Dajuan Wagner graduated from Camden High School before going to college at the University of Memphis. Wagner was the Sixth overall pick in the 2002 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Knee and Ankle Injuries along with a negative reaction to a medication that inflamed his liver derailed his professional career. Wagner played a total of 103 NBA games. 20 Sporting Events That Happened at Boardwalk Hall in Atlantic City YouTube / boxingsgreatest Mike Tyson KO's Michael Spinks One of Mike Tyson's most famous fights was the 91-second Knockout of former champion and previously undefeated Michael Spinks on June 27, 1988, at Boardwalk Hall. YouTube / thatRound, Mike Tyson KO's Larry Holmes Among his title defenses at Boardwalk Hall was a Fourth Round TKO over former champion Larry Holmes on January 22, 1988. Rick Stewart /Allsport Holyfield vs Foreman On April 19, 1991, Undisputed Heavyweight Champion Evander Holyfield defeated former champion George Foreman in his first title defense. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Ward vs Gatti Two of the three fights between Arturo Gatti and Micky Ward took place at Boardwalk Hall. Al Bello /Allsport Sugar Ray Leonard's Final Fight Hector "Macho" Camacho (center) pins Sugar Ray Leonard to the ropes as referee Joe Cotez looks on during a bout in Atlantic City, New Jersey. Camacho won the fight with a TKO in the fifth round on March 1, 1997. YouTube / Uploaded by: Murmurings Of A Boxing Mad Man Roberto Duran vs Iran Barkley AT Boardwalk Hall, Durán knocked Barkley down in the eleventh round and Durán won a split decision (118–112, 116–112, 113–116). The bout was named the 1989 "Fight of the Year" by The Ring. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Mayweather vs Gatti Arturo Gatti is hit by Floyd Mayweather Jr. during their WBC Super Lightweight Championship fight at Boardwalk Hall on June 25, 2005, in Atlantic City, New Jersey. Mayweather Jr. won the fight by way of TKO in the sixth round. Twitter.com/RedditCFB 1964 Liberty Bowl The sixth edition of the Liberty Bowl was played indoors at Boardwalk Hall and featured the Utah Utes and the West Virginia Mountaineers. 6,059 fans attended the game. (Photo by Doug Benc/Getty Images) Boardwalk Bowl Ron Jaworski brought his Philadelphia Soul to play at Boardwalk Hall to face the Las Vegas Outlaws for the venue's first Arena Football League (AFL) game. The Soul won 51–43 with an attendance of 6,514 n May 30, 2015. Mike Gill / TSM AC Blackjacks vs Philadelphia Soul In 2019, the AFL added the Atlantic City Blackjacks with home games at Boardwalk Hall. They finished their inaugural season 4–8 and the entire AFL ceased operations, at the end of the season. A season-high 7,104 fans were in attendance on July 6, 2019. Boardwalkhall.com Atlantic 10 Tournament From 2007 through 2012, the Atlantic 10 Conference held its men's basketball championship at Boardwalk Hall. Mike Gill | TSM Sixers vs Nets, Boardwalk Classic The Philadelphia 76ers played the Brooklyn Nets in a preseason game at Boardwalk Hall on October 13, 2012, in front of 6,887 fans. ( Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images ) Holyfield vs Rahman Hasim Rahman shows a bulge on his forehead due to a broken blood vessel after a headbutt by Evander Holyfield during the heavyweight title fight at the Boardwalk Hall in Atlantic City, New Jersey on June 1, 2002. The fight was stopped after the 8th round in Holyfield's favor after Rahman sustained eye swelling from an accidental head clash. facebook.com/ACBoardwalkBullies AC Boardwalk Bullies win the Kelly Cup In 2003, the team won the Kelly Cup, beating the Columbia Inferno in the finals. Attendance problems led them to be sold and relocated. Getty Images/Al Bello Riddick Bowe vs Andrew Golata II 14 Dec 1996: Andrew Golota delivers a low blow to Riddick Bowe during their return bout at the Atlantic City Convention Centre in Atlantic City, New Jersey. Golata was DQ for repeated low blows in the fight. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Tarver vs. Hopkins On June 10, 2006, Antonio Tarver faced former undisputed world middleweight champion Bernard Hopkins for Tarver's The Ring title at The Boardwalk Hall in Atlantic City, New Jersey. Hopkins, a 3-to-1 underdog, dominated the fight to win a unanimous decision. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Arturo Gatti's Final Fight Gatti attempted a comeback on July 14, 2007, against Alfonso Gomez, only to get TKO'd by Gomez. After the fight, Gatti announced his retirement in the dressing room. Gatti retired with a record of 40 wins and 9 losses, with 31 wins by knockout. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Kelly Pavlik vs Jermain Taylor I ATLANTIC CITY, NJ - SEPTEMBER 29: Kelly Pavlik celebrates after knocking down Jermaine Taylor during their WBC & WBO World Middleweight Championship fight at Boardwalk Hall on September 29, 2007, in Atlantic City, New Jersey. This fight was named Fight of the Year by the Boxing Writers Association of America. https://www.japersrink.com/ Operation Hat Trick On November 24, 2012, Boardwalk Hall hosted "Operation Hat Trick", a charity hockey game to raise money for Hurricane Sandy victims. The game was broadcast live on 97.3 ESPN.
